comparator.name: Bachelor Nanobiology
comparator.institution: Delft University of Technology and Erasmus University Rotterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's current programme page, checked 2026-10-03, states that Nanobiology has used a new curriculum since 2025-2026, with two theory-focus courses and one or two practical courses per quarter in years one and two, professional skills integrated throughout, and teaching divided between TU Delft and Erasmus MC. Its linked official curriculum chart is dated September 2026 and provides course-level credits for the complete 180-EC programme. The current TU Delft and Erasmus University Rotterdam pages identify the joint institutional setting. The exact 2026-2027 allocation is reproduced below.

exception.reason: Nanobiology is an intentionally integrated quantitative life-science degree whose compulsory spine combines molecular and cellular biology with calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, Fourier methods, statistics, mechanics, optics, electricity and magnetism, molecular biophysics, soft matter, scientific programming, computational science, bioinformatics, electronic instrumentation, nanotechnology, two stages of imaging, two stages of laboratory techniques and a 20-EC laboratory research project. UCR offers substantial life science, mathematics, programming, data science and one introductory life-science laboratory course. It does not offer the required physics progression, nanoscale and biophysical integration, scientific instrumentation, experimental biophysics, advanced microscopy and imaging laboratory sequence, nanotechnology practical work, or a comparable 20-EC nanobiology laboratory project. A UCR pathway could study quantitative molecular life science, but it would not be a defensible Nanobiology comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The September 2026 official curriculum chart accounts for the full 180 EC. Year one totals 60 EC across molecular genetics, three mathematics courses, introduction to nanobiology, chemistry, mechanics and optics, programming, biochemistry and structural biology, molecular biophysics, and two practical techniques courses. Year two totals 60 EC across electricity and magnetism, differential equations and Fourier methods, computational sciences, molecular cellular biology, statistics, electronic instruments, evolutionary and developmental biology, two imaging courses, nanotechnology, bioinformatics, soft matter and two science-technology-and-society courses. Year three totals 60 EC through a 30-EC minor, 10 EC of specialist electives and a 20-EC laboratory Bachelor End Project. The live programme page confirms that years one and two deliberately integrate theory and practical work every quarter and that the later curriculum connects physics and biology through microscopy, image analysis, bioinformatics and nanotechnology.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health and Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology and Genetics, HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease and HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology provide relevant biological foundations. HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work involving blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational and Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability and Statistics provide relevant quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA211 Machine Learning and DISDATA212 Image Processing and Computer Vision add computational and general image-analysis perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no mechanics and optics course, electricity and magnetism, molecular or cellular biophysics, soft-matter physics, physical chemistry for nanobiology, electronic scientific instrumentation, nanotechnology laboratory, experimental biophysics techniques, advanced molecular-imaging laboratory, microscopy sequence, or dedicated bioinformatics progression. DISDATA212 addresses general digital image processing and computer vision rather than optical microscopy, instrument physics and biological image formation. HCBLIFE214 is one introductory life-science laboratory, not the target's two-quarter molecular-biology or biophysics techniques sequence followed by nanotechnology, instrumentation, imaging practicals and a 20-EC laboratory research project. UCR's mathematics and computing courses are useful supporting work, but without the compulsory physics, nanoscale measurement and integrated experimental progression the target programme's defining quantitative-biophysical formation is absent. The closest UCR combination would therefore be a broad quantitative molecular-life-science pathway, not an equivalent Nanobiology curriculum.
